biomarkers.name: SDHx (SDHA/B/C/D/AF2) mutations
biomarkers.prevalence: ~30-40% of PPGL have germline SDHx alterations; SDHx alterations are enriched in paraganglioma compared with adrenal pheochromocytoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: SDHB is associated with the highest metastatic risk. SDHD shows parent-of-origin effect (typically paternal transmission) and is often associated with head and neck paraganglioma. Family screening is critical

biomarkers.name: Plasma / urine metanephrines and normetanephrines
biomarkers.prevalence: Elevated in secretory paraganglioma (mostly sympathetic); head/neck paragangliomas are usually non-secretory

biomarkers.name: Dopamine / methoxytyramine
biomarkers.prevalence: Elevated in a subset of dopamine-secreting paragangliomas
biomarkers.clinical_use: Elevated methoxytyramine is associated with SDHx-related disease and metastatic risk

biomarkers.name: SDHB IHC
biomarkers.prevalence: Loss of SDHB staining in SDH-deficient tumours, including SDHx-mutant tumours

biomarkers.name: SSTR2 / 68Ga-DOTATATE PET
biomarkers.prevalence: Frequently strongly positive in head/neck paraganglioma and many SDHx-related tumours
biomarkers.clinical_use: Highly sensitive imaging modality for head/neck and many SDHx-related paragangliomas; can help select patients for PRRT in metastatic disease

biomarkers.name: Genetic panel (as per PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guides screening and family testing; important drivers in PPGL include SDHx genes, VHL, RET, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH, EPAS1, and less commonly HRAS or somatic MAML3 fusion

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: 'Zellballen' architecture identical to pheochromocytoma; extra-adrenal location distinguishes it
variants: head and neck PGL (parasympathetic, usually non-secretory — carotid body, jugulotympanic, vagal, laryngeal)
sympathetic PGL (thoracic, abdominal, pelvic — usually secretory)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: GAPP score has been applied to PGL/PPGL, but there is no fully reliable histologic predictor of metastasis; metastatic disease defines malignancy in current WHO classification

tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Zellballen architecture identical to pheo; extensive vascular network

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Extra-adrenal paraganglia (chief cells) — parasympathetic paraganglia in head/neck (carotid body, jugulotympanic, vagal) or sympathetic paraganglia in thoracoabdominal/pelvic regions
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neural crest — same paraganglionic lineage as pheochromocytoma but extra-adrenal distribution
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Retains paraganglion chief cell differentiation (chromogranin+, synaptophysin+) with sustentacular S100+ cells; often catecholamine-producing if sympathetic (secretory PGL), rarely secretory if parasympathetic (H&N PGL)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Same molecular cluster biology as pheochromocytoma (pseudohypoxia vs kinase signalling); SDHx mutations (especially SDHB) drive pseudohypoxic biology and increased metastatic risk
